title: World Literature Library
description: Explore great stories from around the world — from classic children's tales to young adult literature from every continent.

books.title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
books.author: Lewis Carroll
books.summary: Alice falls down a rabbit hole into a bizarre fantasy world populated by peculiar creatures, a Mad Hatter, a Cheshire Cat, and a tyrannical Queen of Hearts.
discussion: Why does Carroll mix sense and nonsense throughout the story?
How does Alice change from the beginning to the end?

books.title: The Jungle Book
books.author: Rudyard Kipling
books.summary: Mowgli, a boy raised by wolves in the Indian jungle, must survive encounters with the bear Baloo, the panther Bagheera, and the tiger Shere Khan.
discussion: Does Mowgli truly belong with the wolves or with humans?
What does the Law of the Jungle represent?

books.title: The Little Prince
books.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
books.summary: A young prince travels from his tiny asteroid to Earth, meeting various characters. The story explores themes of loneliness, friendship, love, and the loss of childlike wonder in adulthood.
discussion: What does the fox mean when he says 'What is essential is invisible to the eye'?
Why do grown-ups 'never understand anything by themselves'?

books.title: Matilda
books.author: Roald Dahl
books.summary: Matilda is a brilliant child with neglectful parents and an abusive headmistress, Miss Trunchbull. She discovers she has telekinetic powers and uses them to fight back.
discussion: How does reading help Matilda escape her difficult life?
Is it ever right to break the rules like Matilda does?

books.title: The Wind in the Willows
books.author: Kenneth Grahame
books.summary: The adventures of four friends — Mole, Rat, Badger, and the irrepressible Mr Toad — along the banks of an English river.
discussion: What does 'home' mean to Mole in the story?
Is Mr Toad likeable despite his faults? Why?

books.title: Treasure Island
books.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
books.summary: Young Jim Hawkins finds a treasure map and sails to a remote island with a crew that includes the cunning Long John Silver, searching for buried pirate gold.
discussion: Is Long John Silver a villain or an anti-hero?
What does Jim learn about trust?

books.title: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz
books.author: L. Frank Baum
books.summary: Dorothy is swept by a tornado to the magical land of Oz, where she must find the great Wizard to help her return home. She is joined by the Scarecrow, Tin Man, and Cowardly Lion.
discussion: Each character thinks they lack something. Do they really?
What is the significance of 'There's no place like home'?

books.title: The Adventures of Pinocchio
books.author: Carlo Collodi
books.summary: A wooden puppet named Pinocchio is brought to life and goes on adventures, always getting into trouble because of his disobedience, lying, and foolishness — but yearning to become a real boy.
discussion: Why does lying have consequences in this story?
What does it mean to 'become a real boy'?

books.title: The Little Prince
books.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
books.summary: A pilot stranded in the Sahara meets a young prince from a distant asteroid, who shares wisdom about love, friendship, and what truly matters.

books.title: Matilda
books.author: Roald Dahl
books.summary: Telekinetic child prodigy Matilda is neglected by her awful parents and terrorised by the monstrous headmistress Miss Trunchbull, but finds a champion in kind Miss Honey.

books.title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
books.author: J.K. Rowling
books.summary: Orphan Harry Potter discovers on his eleventh birthday that he is a wizard and enrols at Hogwarts School, where he must face the dark wizard Voldemort.

books.title: Comet in Moominland
books.author: Tove Jansson
books.summary: Moomintroll and his friends embark on a journey to find a comet threatening their valley, meeting strange characters along the way.

books.title: The Story of Doctor Dolittle
books.author: Hugh Lofting
books.summary: Dr Dolittle learns to speak to animals from his parrot Polynesia and sets off on an extraordinary voyage to Africa to save a race of monkeys.

books.title: The Jungle Book
books.author: Rudyard Kipling
books.summary: Mowgli, a human child raised by wolves in the Indian jungle, learns the law of the jungle from Baloo the bear and Bagheera the panther, while evading the tiger Shere Khan.

books.title: One Thousand and One Nights
books.author: Various / Traditional
books.summary: A collection of Middle Eastern folk tales told by Scheherazade to delay her execution. Stories include Aladdin, Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves, and Sinbad the Sailor.
discussion: Why is storytelling powerful in this collection?
What makes Scheherazade a hero?

books.title: Anansi the Spider
books.author: West African Oral Tradition
books.summary: Anansi is a spider who uses cleverness and trickery to outwit larger, more powerful animals. He is a cultural hero of the Akan people of Ghana and Caribbean folklore.
discussion: What makes Anansi a good role model despite his tricks?
Why do you think spider stories spread across the African diaspora?

books.title: Panchatantra
books.author: Vishnu Sharma (attributed)
books.summary: The Panchatantra is an ancient Indian collection of interlinked animal fables with moral lessons, written in Sanskrit. It has influenced Aesop's Fables and La Fontaine.
discussion: What is the difference between wisdom and cleverness?
Which fable's lesson do you find most useful in your own life?

books.title: Cinderella: Variations Around the World
books.author: Various
books.summary: The Cinderella story type exists in over 500 versions worldwide: Yeh-Shen (China, 9th century), Aschenputtel (Germany, Grimm), Cendrillon (France, Perrault), Anklet for a Princess (India), Domitila (Mexico). Each reflects its culture's values.
discussion: How does each culture's version reflect its values?
Is the Cinderella story feminist or anti-feminist?

books.title: Anansi Boys
books.author: Neil Gaiman
books.summary: Fat Charlie Nancy discovers his late father was the spider god Anansi and that he has a brother who inherited all their father's magic — based on West African trickster tradition.

books.title: One Thousand and One Nights (Selected Tales)
books.author: Anonymous
books.summary: Scheherazade tells King Shahryar stories over 1001 nights to postpone her execution — including Sinbad, Ali Baba, and Aladdin — weaving tales from Persian, Arab, and Indian traditions.

books.title: The Mahabharata (Retelling)
books.author: C. Rajagopalachari
books.summary: The epic conflict between the Pandava and Kaurava cousins over the kingdom of Hastinapura, containing the Bhagavad Gita — one of Hinduism's most sacred texts.

books.title: The Mwindo Epic
books.author: Cânac Shemwindo (oral tradition)
books.summary: Mwindo, a miraculous child born against his father's wishes, goes on a hero's journey through the underworld and sky world, uniting the human and spirit realms.

books.title: Popol Vuh
books.author: K'iche' Maya (oral tradition)
books.summary: The Maya creation epic: twin hero brothers defeat the lords of the underworld through cunning, and humanity is finally made from maize — the sacred substance of the Americas.

books.title: The Ramayana
books.author: Valmiki
books.summary: Prince Rama's wife Sita is kidnapped by the demon king Ravana, and Rama and his brother Lakshmana embark on an epic quest with the monkey god Hanuman to rescue her.

books.title: Sundiata: An Epic of Old Mali
books.author: D.T. Niane (recorded)
books.summary: The epic of Sundiata Keita — the lion prince who overcame childhood paralysis to defeat the sorcerer king Sumanguru and found the Mali Empire.

books.title: The Epic of Gilgamesh
books.author: Sin-liqe-unninni (attributed)
books.summary: The world's oldest epic: King Gilgamesh, two-thirds divine, quests for immortality after the death of his friend Enkidu — confronting the inevitability of death.

books.title: Anne of Green Gables
books.author: L.M. Montgomery
books.summary: Spirited, red-haired orphan Anne Shirley is mistakenly sent to elderly siblings Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert in Prince Edward Island, Canada. Her imagination, intelligence, and warmth slowly win everyone's hearts.
discussion: How does Anne's imagination help and hinder her?
What does belonging mean to Anne?

books.title: The Secret Garden
books.author: Frances Hodgson Burnett
books.summary: Mary Lennox, a spoilt orphan sent to live in a Yorkshire manor, discovers a locked secret garden and helps it grow again — along with her own transformation.
discussion: How does the garden mirror the changes in Mary?
What role does nature play in mental wellbeing?

books.title: The Diary of a Young Girl
books.author: Anne Frank
books.summary: The real diary of Anne Frank, a Jewish girl who hid with her family in Amsterdam for two years during the Nazi occupation of the Netherlands during World War II. A profound and moving account of humanity, hope, and resilience.
discussion: How does Anne maintain hope in such terrible circumstances?
What does this diary teach us about human resilience?

books.title: The Hobbit
books.author: J.R.R. Tolkien
books.summary: Bilbo Baggins, a comfortable hobbit who wants no adventures, is swept into a quest with a company of dwarves and the wizard Gandalf to reclaim their mountain home from the dragon Smaug.
discussion: How does Bilbo change during the journey?
What is Tolkien saying about greed through the character of Smaug?

books.title: To Kill a Mockingbird
books.author: Harper Lee
books.summary: Scout Finch narrates her childhood in 1930s Alabama, where her father Atticus defends a Black man falsely accused of a crime. A defining novel about racial injustice, empathy, and moral courage.
discussion: What does Atticus mean when he says to climb into someone's skin and walk around in it?
What is the symbolism of the mockingbird?

books.title: The Kite Runner
books.author: Khaled Hosseini
books.summary: Amir, a wealthy Pashtun boy, and Hassan, his Hazara servant and friend, grow up together in Kabul. After a devastating betrayal, Amir's guilt follows him to America and back to Taliban-ruled Afghanistan.
discussion: Is redemption possible after a great betrayal?
How does the setting of Afghanistan affect the story?

books.title: The Perks of Being a Wallflower
books.author: Stephen Chbosky
books.summary: Introverted fifteen-year-old Charlie writes anonymous letters describing his freshman year — finding friendship, music, and confronting repressed trauma.

books.title: The Fault in Our Stars
books.author: John Green
books.summary: Cancer-stricken Hazel meets the charismatic Augustus Waters at a support group, and together they embark on a trip to Amsterdam to find a reclusive author.

books.title: The Alchemist
books.author: Paulo Coelho
books.summary: Andalusian shepherd Santiago follows his recurring dream to the Egyptian pyramids, encountering an alchemist and learning that the treasure was within him all along.

books.title: The Boy in the Striped Pyjamas
books.author: John Boyne
books.summary: Nine-year-old Bruno, son of a Nazi commandant, befriends Jewish boy Shmuel through the fence of Auschwitz — a devastating friendship with a tragic conclusion.

books.title: The Outsiders
books.author: S.E. Hinton
books.summary: Fourteen-year-old Ponyboy Curtis navigates gang rivalries between the Greasers and the Socs in 1960s Tulsa, confronting class, loyalty, and violence.

books.title: Speak
books.author: Laurie Halse Anderson
books.summary: High school freshman Melinda becomes a social outcast after calling the police at a party — slowly revealing through her art teacher's class that she was sexually assaulted.

books.title: Where the Sidewalk Ends
books.author: Shel Silverstein
books.summary: A beloved collection of poems and drawings for children, mixing playfulness, humour, and unexpected wisdom. Topics include imagination, friendship, and the joy of being different.
discussion: Pick a favourite poem and explain why it speaks to you.
How does Silverstein use humour to teach serious lessons?

books.title: Rumi: Selected Poems
books.author: Jalal ad-Din Rumi
books.summary: The 13th-century Persian poet Rumi wrote some of the most beautiful and profound poetry in world literature, exploring themes of love, longing, the divine, and the human soul. His Masnavi is considered the greatest work of Sufi literature.
discussion: What does Rumi mean by 'the reed flute' in his most famous poem?
Why has Rumi's poetry resonated across 800 years and cultures?

books.title: Leaves of Grass
books.author: Walt Whitman
books.summary: Whitman's revolutionary free verse collection celebrates democracy, nature, the body, and American identity — particularly in 'Song of Myself', his 1,336-line masterpiece.

books.title: Duino Elegies
books.author: Rainer Maria Rilke
books.summary: Ten elegies written over a decade explore beauty, loss, angels, and human existence with profound lyrical intensity.

books.title: The Waste Land
books.author: T.S. Eliot
books.summary: A fragmented, multilingual poem of disillusionment after World War I, weaving mythology, Hindu scripture, Shakespeare, and street dialects into a portrait of modern despair.

books.title: The Masnavi (selected)
books.author: Jalal ad-Din Rumi
books.summary: Rumi's six-book spiritual masterpiece of 25,000 verses tells stories, debates theology, and uses mystical poetry to describe the soul's longing for divine union.

books.title: Gitanjali (Song Offerings)
books.author: Rabindranath Tagore
books.summary: Tagore's devotional poetry of 103 prose poems, expressing the relationship between the human soul and the divine through imagery of seasons, rivers, and music.

books.title: Pride and Prejudice
books.author: Jane Austen
books.summary: Elizabeth Bennet navigates love, class, and marriage in Regency England, sparring wittily with the proud Mr Darcy before both realise their initial judgements were wrong.

books.title: The Great Gatsby
books.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
books.summary: Nick Carraway narrates the story of the mysterious, wealthy Jay Gatsby and his obsession with the American Dream and his lost love Daisy Buchanan in 1920s New York.

books.title: Jane Eyre
books.author: Charlotte Brontë
books.summary: Orphaned Jane Eyre grows up to become a governess and falls in love with the brooding Mr Rochester, uncovering a dark secret that threatens their happiness.

books.title: Crime and Punishment
books.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
books.summary: A destitute student Raskolnikov murders a pawnbroker, believing himself above moral law, then suffers intense psychological torment and eventual redemption.

books.title: Anna Karenina
books.author: Leo Tolstoy
books.summary: Russian aristocrat Anna Karenina abandons her husband for the dashing Count Vronsky, triggering social ruin and tragedy in 19th-century St Petersburg.

books.title: Don Quixote
books.author: Miguel de Cervantes
books.summary: An aging country gentleman, driven mad by reading too many chivalric romances, sets out as a 'knight errant' with his squire Sancho Panza on absurd adventures.

books.title: Les Misérables
books.author: Victor Hugo
books.summary: Ex-convict Jean Valjean is relentlessly pursued by Inspector Javert across revolutionary 19th-century France in an epic story of justice, redemption, and love.

books.title: War and Peace
books.author: Leo Tolstoy
books.summary: Five aristocratic families navigate Napoleon's invasion of Russia, interweaving personal romance and philosophical reflection with epic historical battle scenes.

books.title: Brave New World
books.author: Aldous Huxley
books.summary: In a future where humans are engineered for happiness and conformity, Bernard Marx questions whether a comfortable life without freedom is worth living.

books.title: To Kill a Mockingbird
books.author: Harper Lee
books.summary: Young Scout Finch watches her lawyer father Atticus defend a Black man falsely accused of a crime in 1930s Alabama, confronting racial injustice head-on.

books.title: Things Fall Apart
books.author: Chinua Achebe
books.summary: Okonkwo, a proud Igbo warrior, resists the arrival of European missionaries and colonialism, leading to tragic conflict between tradition and change.

books.title: Weep Not, Child
books.author: Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o
books.summary: Young Njoroge's dreams of education are shattered by the Mau Mau uprising as Kenya struggles for independence from British colonial rule.

books.title: Purple Hibiscus
books.author: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
books.summary: Fifteen-year-old Kambili lives under her fanatically religious father's control in post-colonial Nigeria, finding freedom through her aunt's liberal household.

books.title: So Long a Letter
books.author: Mariama Bâ
books.summary: A recently widowed Senegalese woman writes a letter to her best friend, reflecting on marriage, betrayal, and women's lives in West African society.

books.title: Season of Migration to the North
books.author: Tayeb Salih
books.summary: A Sudanese man returns from Oxford to find his village transformed, and uncovers the mysterious story of Mustafa Sa'eed, who lived a dark double life in London.

books.title: God's Bits of Wood
books.author: Ousmane Sembène
books.summary: The 1947–48 railway workers' strike in French West Africa becomes an epic of collective resistance, as women play an increasingly central role in the movement.

books.title: The Famished Road
books.author: Ben Okri
books.summary: Spirit child Azaro, born to die and return, chooses to stay in the world of the living in a Nigerian slum, moving between the spirit world and modern poverty.

books.title: Disgrace
books.author: J.M. Coetzee
books.summary: A Cape Town professor loses his career after an affair with a student, retreats to his daughter's rural farm, and confronts post-apartheid South Africa's violence.

books.title: The Tale of Genji
books.author: Murasaki Shikibu
books.summary: The world's first novel follows the romantic adventures of Hikaru Genji, the son of a Japanese emperor, through the elegant court life of Heian-era Japan.

books.title: The Kite Runner
books.author: Khaled Hosseini
books.summary: Amir betrays his loyal friend Hassan in 1970s Kabul, then must return decades later to Taliban-controlled Afghanistan to find redemption.

books.title: Kitchen
books.author: Banana Yoshimoto
books.summary: A young Japanese woman copes with grief after losing her last relative, finding solace in kitchens and unexpected friendship in contemporary Tokyo.

books.title: A Thousand Splendid Suns
books.author: Khaled Hosseini
books.summary: Two Afghan women from different generations, bound by fate and friendship, endure decades of war, loss, and oppression in 20th-century Afghanistan.

books.title: In the Pond
books.author: Ha Jin
books.summary: A worker in a Chinese factory town becomes obsessed with gaining an apartment for his family, resorting to increasingly absurd methods to fight bureaucratic injustice.

books.title: Interpreter of Maladies
books.author: Jhumpa Lahiri
books.summary: Nine stories of Indian and Indian-American characters navigating cultural displacement, failed marriages, and the search for connection and identity.

books.title: Snow Country
books.author: Yasunari Kawabata
books.summary: A wealthy Tokyo dilettante travels to a mountain hot-spring resort in the Japanese Alps and falls for a local geisha in a doomed relationship.

books.title: The House of the Spirits
books.author: Isabel Allende
books.summary: Four generations of the Trueba family are bound together by magical powers, political upheaval, and love in 20th-century Chile — a multi-generational epic.

books.title: One Hundred Years of Solitude
books.author: Gabriel García Márquez
books.summary: The Buendía family founds the town of Macondo and endures one hundred years of magical events, wars, plagues, and loves in García Márquez's defining masterpiece.

books.title: Love in the Time of Cholera
books.author: Gabriel García Márquez
books.summary: Florentino Ariza waits 51 years for Fermina Daza — refusing all other loves — and finally declares his passion after her husband's death in Caribbean South America.

books.title: Ficciones
books.author: Jorge Luis Borges
books.summary: Seventeen labyrinthine short stories exploring infinite libraries, circular time, labyrinths, and fictional encyclopaedias — mind-bending literary puzzles that defy genre.

books.title: The Brief Wondrous Life of Oscar Wao
books.author: Junot Díaz
books.summary: Oscar, an obese sci-fi-loving nerd from New Jersey, pursues love while his family carries the 'fukú' — a curse tied to the Trujillo dictatorship in the Dominican Republic.

books.title: Pedro Páramo
books.author: Juan Rulfo
books.summary: Juan Preciado travels to the ghost town of Comala to find his father Pedro Páramo, only to discover a village of whispers, memories, and the dead.

books.title: Like Water for Chocolate
books.author: Laura Esquivel
books.summary: Tita, the youngest daughter forbidden to marry, pours her emotions into magical meals that affect everyone who eats them across early 20th-century Mexico.

books.title: Kiss of the Spider Woman
books.author: Manuel Puig
books.summary: Two prisoners — a gay window dresser and a Marxist revolutionary — share a cell in 1970s Buenos Aires, bonding through film descriptions and politics.

books.title: The Metamorphosis
books.author: Franz Kafka
books.summary: Gregor Samsa wakes to find himself transformed into a giant insect, and the story follows his family's gradual estrangement from — and relief at losing — their changed son.

books.title: Madame Bovary
books.author: Gustave Flaubert
books.summary: Emma Bovary, a romantic dreamer trapped in a dull marriage to a provincial French doctor, pursues affairs and luxury that lead to tragic ruin.

books.title: The Brothers Karamazov
books.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
books.summary: Three brothers — the sensual Dmitri, the intellectual Ivan, and the spiritual Alyosha — become entangled in their father's murder and a philosophical battle over faith.

books.title: Death in Venice
books.author: Thomas Mann
books.summary: Ageing writer Gustav von Aschenbach travels to Venice and becomes obsessed with the beautiful boy Tadzio, trapped as cholera spreads through the city.

books.title: Siddhartha
books.author: Hermann Hesse
books.summary: A young Brahmin in ancient India leaves home to seek enlightenment, passing through asceticism, sensuality, and materialism before finding peace by a river.

books.title: The Plague
books.author: Albert Camus
books.summary: A plague descends on the Algerian town of Oran, trapping its citizens. Doctor Rieux's resistance to the epidemic is Camus's allegory of fighting absurdity and evil.

books.title: Nineteen Eighty-Four
books.author: George Orwell
books.summary: Winston Smith works for Big Brother's totalitarian regime rewriting history, and risks everything for love and rebellion — coining 'doublethink', 'thoughtcrime', and 'unperson'.

books.title: Steppenwolf
books.author: Hermann Hesse
books.summary: The alienated intellectual Harry Haller believes he is half-man, half-wolf, unable to fit into bourgeois society — until he enters the magical Tratment and is transformed.

books.title: Midnight's Children
books.author: Salman Rushdie
books.summary: Saleem Sinai is born at the exact moment of Indian independence and is telepathically linked to all children born in that midnight hour in Rushdie's magical epic of modern India.

books.title: The White Tiger
books.author: Aravind Adiga
books.summary: Ambitious Balram Halwai narrates his rise from servant to entrepreneur by murdering his employer — a darkly comic critique of modern India's class system.

books.title: The Remains of the Day
books.author: Kazuo Ishiguro
books.summary: English butler Stevens recalls his service to Lord Darlington and his suppressed feelings for housekeeper Miss Kenton on a drive through the English countryside.

books.title: Never Let Me Go
books.author: Kazuo Ishiguro
books.summary: Kathy, Ruth, and Tommy are students at the idyllic Hailsham boarding school — and clones raised to donate their organs. A quiet, devastating dystopian love story.

books.title: The God of Small Things
books.author: Arundhati Roy
books.summary: Twins Rahel and Estha return to Kerala to face the events of 1969 that destroyed their family — a forbidden love transgressing India's caste boundaries.

books.title: My Brilliant Friend
books.author: Elena Ferrante
books.summary: The first of the Neapolitan Novels follows Elena and the brilliant, fierce Lila through childhood in a violent Naples neighbourhood in the 1950s.

books.title: The Power of the Dog
books.author: Thomas Savage
books.summary: Brutal, brilliant Montana rancher Phil Burbank torments his brother's new wife and her sensitive son in a 1920s Western that probes masculinity and cruelty.

books.title: Half of a Yellow Sun
books.author: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
books.summary: Twin sisters and their lovers navigate love, loyalty, and survival during the Biafran War (1967–70) — Nigeria's devastating civil war largely forgotten by the West.

books.title: The Shadow of the Wind
books.author: Carlos Ruiz Zafón
books.summary: In 1940s Barcelona, young Daniel discovers a book by the mysterious Julian Carax and becomes obsessed with finding the author — only to discover someone is burning all Carax's books.

books.title: Oryx and Crake
books.author: Margaret Atwood
books.summary: Snowman, possibly the last human, recalls how his brilliant friend Crake engineered a plague that wiped out humanity, in Atwood's prophetic biotech dystopia.

books.title: Norwegian Wood
books.author: Haruki Murakami
books.summary: Toru Watanabe recalls his college years in 1960s Tokyo, his love for the fragile Naoko and her mental illness, and his growing feelings for the vivacious Midori.

books.title: The Bonesetter's Daughter
books.author: Amy Tan
books.summary: Ruth Young discovers her Chinese mother LuLing's memoir, unlocking a hidden family history stretching back to rural China and a secret about her grandmother.

books.title: Season of Migration Retold
books.author: Rabih Alameddine
books.summary: A Lebanese doctor connects fragmented stories of AIDS deaths in San Francisco with the Lebanese civil war, narrated by a sardonic god.

books.title: American Gods
books.author: Neil Gaiman
books.summary: Ex-convict Shadow Moon travels across America with the mysterious Mr Wednesday — Odin in disguise — as old gods of myth battle new gods of technology and media.

books.title: The Tale of Peter Rabbit
books.author: Beatrix Potter
books.summary: Peter Rabbit disobeys his mother and sneaks into Mr. McGregor's garden, where he gets into all sorts of trouble. This classic picture book teaches children about consequences and the importance of listening to parents. Peter barely escapes and returns home exhausted but wiser.
moral_lessons: Curiosity must be balanced with caution
discussion_questions: Why did Peter disobey his mother?
What would you have done differently?
What did Peter learn at the end?

books.title: The Tale of Jemima Puddle-Duck
books.author: Beatrix Potter
books.summary: Jemima Puddle-Duck wants to hatch her own eggs but is tricked by a sly fox who pretends to help. The fox's true plan is revealed just in time. This story teaches children to recognize deception and the importance of trusting wise friends.
moral_lessons: Not everyone who offers help has good intentions
discussion_questions: How did the fox trick Jemima?
Who saved Jemima and why?

books.title: The Tale of Squirrel Nutkin
books.author: Beatrix Potter
books.summary: Squirrel Nutkin repeatedly teases Old Brown the owl with riddles while his brother squirrels politely gather nuts. His impertinence eventually leads to a frightening consequence. This classic teaches children about politeness and respect.
discussion_questions: Why was Nutkin's behaviour rude?
Was the punishment fair?

books.title: Winnie-the-Pooh
books.author: A.A. Milne
books.summary: Pooh Bear and his friends in the Hundred Acre Wood have gentle adventures involving honey, friendship, and imagination. Each chapter presents a small problem solved with kindness and creativity. The stories celebrate the magic of childhood friendship.
moral_lessons: Imagination makes every day an adventure
discussion_questions: Who is your favourite character and why?
How do the friends help each other?

books.title: The House at Pooh Corner
books.author: A.A. Milne
books.summary: In the sequel to Winnie-the-Pooh, the friends build Eeyore a house and welcome Tigger to the Hundred Acre Wood. The gentle adventures continue with warmth and wit. The final chapter, where Christopher Robin must leave for school, is one of literature's most moving childhood farewells.
moral_lessons: Friends support each other through change
Saying goodbye is part of life's journey
discussion_questions: How do the friends welcome Tigger?
Why is the ending bittersweet?

books.title: The Complete Fairy Tales
books.author: Hans Christian Andersen
books.summary: Andersen wrote over 150 fairy tales including The Little Mermaid, The Ugly Duckling, Thumbelina, and The Snow Queen. Unlike collected folk tales, these were original stories with deeper emotional truth. Many end sadly, teaching that life is complex and beauty comes in unexpected forms.
moral_lessons: Sacrifice for love requires great courage
discussion_questions: What does the Ugly Duckling teach about judging others?
Is the Little Mermaid's sacrifice worth it?

books.title: Grimm's Fairy Tales
books.author: Brothers Grimm
books.summary: Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm collected German folk tales including Cinderella, Snow White, Rumpelstiltskin, Hansel and Gretel, and Rapunzel. Originally intended for scholars, these tales have become beloved children's classics. The stories often deal with courage, cleverness, and overcoming evil.
discussion_questions: What makes a fairy tale different from a regular story?
Which tale has the most important lesson for today?

books.title: Aesop's Fables
books.author: Aesop
books.summary: Aesop's fables are short stories featuring animals that illustrate moral lessons. Famous fables include The Tortoise and the Hare, The Boy Who Cried Wolf, The Ant and the Grasshopper, and The Fox and the Grapes. Each story ends with a moral that applies to human behavior.
moral_lessons: Slow and steady wins the race
Honesty is always the best policy
discussion_questions: Which fable has the most important lesson?
Can you invent your own fable?

books.title: Just So Stories
books.author: Rudyard Kipling
books.summary: Kipling's playful creation stories explain how animals got their distinctive features: how the elephant got its trunk, how the camel got its hump, why the leopard has spots. Told with rhythmic language and sly humor, these stories celebrate curiosity about the natural world.
moral_lessons: There are many ways to tell a story
discussion_questions: Which Just So Story is your favourite explanation?
Can you write a Just So Story of your own?

books.title: The Jungle Book
books.author: Rudyard Kipling
books.summary: Mowgli is a boy raised by wolves in the Indian jungle, befriended by the bear Baloo, the panther Bagheera, and threatened by the tiger Shere Khan. The stories explore what it means to belong to two worlds and the laws that govern life in the wild.
moral_lessons: We can belong to more than one world
Laws and codes exist for good reasons
